documents.title: Artificial Intelligence Guidelines, Clark Atlanta University (CAU AI Guidelines)
documents.summary: Guidelines from the CAU AI Task Force asking every instructor to put an AI policy on the syllabus and choose among Open, Limited or No Use, with considerations for each and recommended syllabus wording.
documents.stance_why: The guidelines set no university-wide rule: "the decision to incorporate these technologies ... is at the discretion of the instructor" and each instructor picks Open Use, Limited Use or No Use.

units.why: The preamble says "All instructors should have an AI course policy included on their syllabus", a syllabus-statement requirement addressed to instructors, so P09 rather than a stance type.
units.anchor: All instructors should have an AI course policy included on their syllabus.

units.why: States the aim "to prepare scholars for the AI-driven workforce"; the workforce-preparation reason is the careers rationale, P44, not a framework preamble.
units.anchor: to prepare scholars for the AI-driven workforce

units.why: Frames generative AI as "part of our educational toolbox, just as dictionaries, calculators, and web searches", treating AI like an ordinary outside tool; closest fit is P45 (AI like other sources), and the framing leans welcoming.
units.anchor: Generative AI tools, such as ChatGPT, can be part of our educational toolbox

units.why: Defines generative AI as something that "can be used to create new content in response to prompts" including text, solutions, images; a definition setting scope, P61.
units.anchor: Generative AI can be used to create new content in response to prompts.

units.why: Says the decision to incorporate AI "is at the discretion of the instructor"; this hands the rule to each instructor, P04.
units.anchor: is at the discretion of the instructor

units.why: Names "Open Use, Limited Use, and No Use" as the course AI Use Options, a named tier scheme, P05.
units.anchor: These course AI Use Options include Open Use, Limited Use, and No Use.
units.frag_start: These course AI Use Options include

units.why: "It is the responsibility of the scholars to adhere to the guidelines established by their course instructor" makes students answerable for following the course rule; no type is about adherence exactly, so P29 (students' responsibility) is chosen.
units.anchor: It is the responsibility of the scholars to adhere to the guidelines

units.why: Instructors "should decide whether, when, and how AI should be used" and tell students on the first day; the first-day communication duty is P09 rather than P04 because the focus is communicating boundaries.
units.anchor: clearly communicate those boundaries to scholars on the first day of class

units.why: "intellectual honesty and transparency about the use of AI is paramount" asks for transparency about AI use, i.e. acknowledgment, P24.
units.anchor: intellectual honesty and transparency about the use of AI is paramount

units.why: Instructors "should select an AI Use Option category for each of their courses", a duty to state a category per course, P09 (the tiers themselves are P05).
units.anchor: Instructors should select an AI Use Option category for each of their courses.

units.why: Warns "most AI content detectors are not 100% reliable", a statement that detectors are unreliable, P39.
units.anchor: most AI content detectors are not 100% reliable

units.why: Open Use is defined as AI tools for "any stage or phase of work", a default allowing AI broadly, P02.
units.anchor: for any stage or phase of work in this class

units.why: "In all situations, usage of AI tools should be cited" under Open Use; a citation duty, P24.
units.anchor: In all situations, usage of AI tools should be cited.
units.frag_start: In all situations, usage of AI
units.policy: Under Open Use, usage of AI tools should be cited.

units.why: "Discussion and examples on the ethical use of AI tools" is a consideration for Open Use courses; teaching ethics fits P53 best.
units.anchor: Discussion and examples on the ethical use of AI tools

units.why: "Strategies for using AI tools responsibly" is a consideration for Open Use syllabi; teaching responsible use as a skill, P44.
units.anchor: Strategies for using AI tools responsibly

units.why: "Grading criteria for AI-assisted work" is listed as a consideration, meaning grading is adapted to AI, P35.
units.anchor: Grading criteria for AI-assisted work

units.why: "Guidelines for proper citation of AI-assisted work" is a consideration for Open Use syllabi, a citation matter, P24.
units.anchor: Guidelines for proper citation of AI-assisted work

units.why: Limited Use permits "specific AI tools" or "specific coursework", a narrow permission, so tiering P05 rather than P02.
units.anchor: Limited Use is the permission to use specific AI tools for any coursework

units.why: The Limited Use paragraph repeats "usage of AI tools should be cited"; kept as a tier-specific citation duty, P24.
units.anchor: In all situations, usage of AI tools should be cited.
units.policy: Under Limited Use, usage of AI tools should be cited.

units.why: "Specific instances where AI use is permitted" asks instructors to list allowed uses in the syllabus, P09.
units.anchor: Specific instances where AI use is permitted

units.why: "Disclosure requirements for AI-assisted coursework" is a consideration, P24.
units.anchor: Disclosure requirements for AI-assisted coursework

units.why: "Consequences for unauthorized AI use" should be stated, i.e. penalties in advance, P37.
units.anchor: Consequences for unauthorized AI use

units.why: No Use is "the prohibited use of AI tools in this course", a ban, P01.
units.anchor: No Use is the prohibited use of AI tools in this course.

units.why: "Clarification of what constitutes AI tools (to avoid ambiguity)" asks to define AI tools for scope, P61.
units.anchor: Clarification of what constitutes AI tools (to avoid ambiguity)

units.why: "Consequences for violating the AI class policy" for No Use courses; stated penalties, P37.
units.anchor: Consequences for violating the AI class policy

units.why: "Strategies for completing coursework in class to AI-proof your coursework" shifts work to in-class unassisted settings, P33.
units.anchor: Strategies for completing coursework in class to

units.why: "Strategies for detecting AI usage and protocols for addressing suspected AI use" concerns detection; P40.
units.anchor: Strategies for detecting AI usage and protocols for addressing suspected AI use

units.why: "Alternative resources and support for coursework" in No Use courses; nearest type P51 (alternatives exist).
units.anchor: Alternative resources and support for coursework

units.why: Recommended verbiage says "Courses are either Open Use, Limited Use, or No Use. This course is ____", telling students the category on the syllabus; P09.
units.anchor: Courses are either Open Use, Limited Use, or No Use.

units.why: States that AI usage considerations "vary by course", i.e. each course's policy governs only that course, P11.
units.anchor: usage considerations at Clark Atlanta University vary by course.

units.why: "Scholars are responsible for reviewing and adhering to the specific AI usage guidelines" in the syllabus; student duty to follow the course policy, P29 as responsibility.
units.anchor: Scholars are responsible for reviewing and adhering to the specific AI usage guidelines

units.why: "Any student who is unsure ... must consult their instructor prior to utilization" is the ask-first rule, P10.
units.anchor: must consult their instructor prior to utilization

documents.title: Clark Atlanta University Sample Syllabus Template
documents.summary: Official sample syllabus template with a single placeholder section directing faculty to the AI Guidelines and to insert their AI-use expectations.
documents.stance_why: The template only says faculty should insert their AI-use expectations in this section, leaving the decision to instructors.

units.why: The template says "Faculty should consult the CAU Artificial Intelligence Guidelines document and then insert their AI-Use expectations in this section", a requirement that the syllabus state AI expectations, P09.
units.anchor: Faculty should consult the CAU Artificial Intelligence Guidelines document

notes: Course layer deferred in collect file. Guidelines list considerations as bullets; coded as instructor-facing prompts.
